hints: Look at the balanced equation and count the total moles of gas on each side to predict the pressure effect.
Notice there are 2 moles of $\text{HI(g)}$ on the left and 1 + 1 = 2 moles of gas on the right, so pressure cannot favour either side.
Remember $\Delta H = +12 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ means the forward decomposition is endothermic, so adding heat will favour that direction.
walkthrough:
**Count the gas moles on each side**

Think of pressure as the system trying to reduce crowding. More pressure favours the side with fewer gas molecules.

$$2\text{HI(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{I}_2\text{(g)} + \text{H}_2\text{(g)}$$
Left: 2 moles. Right: 1 + 1 = 2 moles.

**Apply Le Chatelier to pressure**

Because both sides have the same number of gas moles, increasing pressure increases both sides equally.

There is no shift to reduce moles, so there is no change in position of equilibrium.

**Apply Le Chatelier to temperature**

Think of heat as a reactant or product. Here $\Delta H$ is positive, so the forward reaction takes in heat.

$$\text{heat} + 2\text{HI} \rightleftharpoons \text{I}_2 + \text{H}_2$$
Increasing temperature adds heat, so the system uses it up by moving to the right, making more $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{H}_2$.

options.A: Incorrect. Increasing temperature does move the equilibrium to the right because the forward reaction is endothermic, but increasing pressure does not. With equal gas moles on both sides, pressure has no effect.
options.B: Incorrect on both counts. Pressure has no effect when gas moles are equal, not a shift right. Temperature shifts right for an endothermic forward reaction, not left.
options.C: Correct and well done. Equal moles of gas (2 on each side) means no change with pressure, and a positive $\Delta H$ means the endothermic forward direction is favoured when temperature is increased, so equilibrium moves to the right.
options.D: Half right but half wrong. No change with pressure is correct, but increasing temperature for an endothermic forward reaction moves equilibrium to the right, not to the left. Left would be correct only if the forward reaction were exothermic.
